findings.evidence: Lines 106-107 and 136-137 are character-identical apart from the hypothesis name (`h.2 _` vs `h'.2 _`). The lemmas are real: `Finset.subtype_mem_eq_attach` at upstream/mathlib/Mathlib/Data/Finset/Image.lean:667, `Finsupp.support_subtypeDomain`/`subtypeDomain_apply` at Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Basic.lean:792,796. The scaffolding is needed because `Matrix.PosSemidef` quantifies over `n →₀ R` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/PosDef.lean:62-63); Mathlib itself duplicates the same block at Mathlib/Analysis/Matrix/Order.lean:231 and :250, so no upstream lemma covers it.
findings.fix: Factor it into one lemma in this file, e.g. `lemma posSemidef_of_forall_submatrix_support {M : Matrix n n R} (hM : M.IsHermitian) (h : ∀ x : n →₀ R, (M.submatrix ((↑) : x.support → n) (↑)).PosSemidef) : M.PosSemidef`, carrying the `simpa` once; both `map_re` and the `mpr` branch of `posSemidef_map_ofReal_iff` then reduce to supplying the `Fintype`-case PSD witness. Since the file's implementation note already flags it for upstreaming, this is also the lemma Mathlib is missing.
findings.issue: `PosSemidef.map_re` (lines 100-107) and `posSemidef_map_ofReal_iff` (lines 126-137) each open-code the same reduction from the `n →₀ 𝕜` quadratic form to the `Fintype` case on `x.support`: `classical`, `h.submatrix ((↑) : x.support → n)`, then the identical two-line `simpa [Finsupp.sum, ← Finset.sum_attach x.support, ← Finset.subtype_mem_eq_attach, ← Finsupp.subtypeDomain_apply, ← Finsupp.support_subtypeDomain] using _.2 _` at lines 106-107 and 136-137. That reusable fact — a hermitian matrix all of whose support submatrices are PSD is PSD — is hidden inside two proofs, and the reduction rests on a four-lemma reversed-`simp` set that breaks if any of those Finsupp/Finset lemmas is renamed or restated.

summary: The prior round's findings are resolved: hermiticity is now the single lemma `conj_mat_apply`, and the real-part transfers go through explicit `mat_re_apply`/`f1_re`/`g1_re` rewrites rather than bare defeq. One issue remains: the Finsupp-support reduction used to prove positive semidefiniteness over a general index type is copied verbatim in both new transfer lemmas instead of being factored out.
